Verdict: TRUE_POSITIVE
Confidence: HIGH
Reasoning: The code uses `filepath.Join(dst, entry.Header.Name)` to construct the target path for extraction without verifying that the resulting path remains within the intended destination directory. A malicious tar entry with a name containing relative path traversal sequences (e.g., `../../../etc/passwd`) will cause files to be written outside of `dst`, enabling arbitrary file overwrite or creation. This is the classic "Zip Slip" / path traversal vulnerability in archive extraction logic.
RealCWE: CWE-22
SuggestedFix: After computing `target` with `filepath.Join`, resolve it to an absolute path and verify it is prefixed by the destination directory before performing any filesystem operation. For example: `absDst, _ := filepath.Abs(dst); absTarget, _ := filepath.Abs(target); if !strings.HasPrefix(absTarget, absDst+string(os.PathSeparator)) { return fmt.Errorf("path traversal detected: %q", entry.Header.Name) }`. Additionally, sanitize or reject entries containing leading `/` or `..` components.

This approach is vulnerable to path traversal bypass because sequences such as `....//` collapse into `../` after the replacement, allowing an attacker to write files outside the intended directory. Additionally, ensure all expected file extensions are validated before writing the file, rather than only after.
